reasoning: A hybrid approach combines autonomous reasoning to identify common syntactic features across misclassified instances with XAI tools to quantify their model-level importance. This ensures both semantic grounding and statistical validation of potential spurious correlations. The shared feature must appear across all instances and be highly attributed by the model, making joint reasoning and quantitative attribution essential.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which columns are present in all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 29328) and list their values across each instance.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of columns that appear in all three instances with their corresponding values

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared column (e.g., marital-status, education, age) has a semantically plausible relationship to the target class (>50K vs <=50K), or if it may be a spurious correlation based on domain knowledge.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of candidate features flagged as potentially spurious due to lack of semantic relevance to class, despite high correlation in the model

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides global feature importance with interpretability, enabling detection of features with high attribution across all misclassified instances. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local explanations to validate contributions for each instance, while sensitivity analysis isolates feature impact by removal. Together, they validate whether a shared column has spurious high influence, independent of semantic relevance, particularly in instances with unknown ground truth.
